what_its_for: Gemfibrozil is used to lower high triglycerides (a type of fat) in your blood and to raise your 'good' cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart disease and pancreatitis (painful inflammation of the pancreas) caused by very high triglyceride levels.
how_to_take: Take gemfibrozil by mouth with a full glass of water. It is very important to take it 30 minutes BEFORE breakfast and 30 minutes BEFORE dinner (twice a day). Taking it at the right time helps it work best. You can take it with or without food, but taking it before meals works better. Swallow the tablet whole.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 600 mg taken twice a day — once about 30 minutes before breakfast and once about 30 minutes before your evening meal. Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribed. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how your body responds to the medication.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still close to the time you were supposed to take it. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store gemfibrozil at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking gemfibrozil together with certain cholesterol-lowering drugs called statins (like simvastatin or lovastatin) unless your doctor specifically approves it, as this combination can cause serious muscle damage. Avoid alcohol, as it can raise your triglyceride levels and make the medication less effective. Limit fatty, greasy, and sugary foods since they raise triglycerides. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medications you take, especially blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), because gemfibrozil can make blood thinners stronger.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, or cramps (especially with fever or dark-colored urine — this could be a sign of serious muscle breakdown called rhabdomyolysis); stomach or abdominal pain; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); signs of gallstones such as severe pain in your upper right abdomen; unusual bleeding or bruising; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if you develop any new or unusual symptoms while taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Gemfibrozil starts working within a few days, but it may take 4 to 8 weeks of regular use before you notice a significant improvement in your triglyceride and cholesterol levels. Your doctor will order blood tests to check how well the medication is working. Keep taking it even if you feel fine — high triglycerides usually have no symptoms. Diet, exercise, and weight loss are also important parts of your treatment.
special_populations: Kidney or liver disease: Gemfibrozil is NOT recommended if you have severe kidney or liver disease. Your doctor will check your kidney and liver function before and during treatment. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. The safety of gemfibrozil during pregnancy is not well established; your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits. Breastfeeding: It is not known if gemfibrozil passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects, especially muscle problems. Children: Gemfibrozil is generally not recommended for children unless specifically directed by a doctor.
